findings.title: Immediate cancellations still fill SendGrid's pending-cancellation limit
findings.body: When `immediateDelete` is true, this sends the SendGrid cancel request immediately and returns without setting `cancelled=true`. Rescheduling uses this path, as do workflow/step deletion, so far-future sends remain in SendGrid's pending-cancellation queue until their scheduled dates—the limit of 100 that this PR is intended to avoid can still be reached. Once reached, later cancellations can fail and reminders may be sent. If the request fails, the error is swallowed and the cron has no `cancelled` flag to retry. These cancellations need to use the deferred cancellation flow or otherwise ensure they are cleaned up and retried.

findings.title: One failed cancellation aborts the rest of the cron batch
findings.body: The `try` covers the entire loop, so a single failed SendGrid request exits the loop and skips every later cancelled reminder in the batch. Those reminders remain pending at SendGrid; if one becomes due before the next cron run, the initial cleanup at lines 34–41 deletes its database row before it can be retried, and the email can be sent. Handle failures per reminder or ensure due cancelled reminders are processed before cleanup.
